messages:
andrea: quick heads-up — observed a perf regression on FA-v3 causal path when head_dim % 8 != 0 on H100. small repro attached, ~25% slower than v2 fallback for seqlen 512. anyone seen this?

mike: can you paste the microbench numbers? is this only causal or non-causal too?

andrea: causal only so far. repro command I used:
```
./perf_probe --model llama-13b --kernel-candidates flashattn_v3,sdpa_v2,naive --heads 17 --head-dim 64 --seq-len 512 --gpu H100 --batch 4
```
metrics: flashattn_v3_causal -> 1700 tok/s, sdpa_v2_noncausal (fallback) -> 2300 tok/s, naive -> 1200 tok/s

sophia: unexpected — head count 17 means QKV packing misaligns with v3 tile size. FA-v3 expects head groups that align to 8/16 in our implementation. v2 had a more tolerant tiling. cc @jason

jason: looking at autotuner logs, we probed kernels but the selector favored fa_v3 for latency estimate because of a bad probe for short warmup. snippet from tuner log:
```
PROBE kernel=flashattn_v3 causal seqlen=512 heads=17 head_dim=64  est=12.3ms  sample=14.8ms
PROBE kernel=sdpa_v2  causal seqlen=512 heads=17 head_dim=64  est=15.0ms  sample=12.7ms
SELECT flashattn_v3
```
so estimator underpredicted variance for fa_v3. we need hysteresis or resample.

laura: also noticed KV cache misindexing on the fa_v3 path when head groups are uneven — KV stride calc uses head_group = heads // 2 in a couple places (old hack). That produces odd offsets for head counts that don't divide cleanly.

andrea: here's a quick patch I tried in local: force fa_v3 to run only when heads % 8 == 0 or head_dim % 16 == 0. With that rule the autotuner falls back to sdpa_v2 and perf matches prior numbers. But it's a blunt instrument.

mike: can we instead add a probe-resample if probe variance > 10%? or use a lightweight microprofile (10 iters) after first selected kernel and rollback if throughput < threshold?

jason: yeah, implement a post-select verification step. have autotuner do N=10 warmup / 20 sample iters and compare to predicted. if diff > 20% mark probe noisy and re-evaluate. also add architecture tag: prefer sdpa_v2 on A100-family for odd-head counts; prefer fa_v3 on H100 only if aligned.

sophia: note: H100 has different tensor core layout so fa_v3 speedups are larger when alignment matches. but misaligned tiling causes extra memcopies and >1ms jitter per token. we should add a telemetry tag to capture "head_alignment" for future rollouts.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: autotuner/hysteresis-fallback @staging — build #7823 — link: https://ci.redwood/d/7823

andrea: I'll open a PR with resample logic + telemetry + an integration test that runs head counts [15,16,17,18] across A100/H100. putting perf numbers in the PR description.

mike: thanks. can we also add a small experiment to the caching layer? if KV cache stride mismatches, we should disable fa_v3 entirely for that session and record a diagnostic.

laura: agreed. I'll add a KV stride check in runtime init and emit a tagged metric: runtime.kernel_reject_reason = "kv_stride_unaligned"

andrea: sweet. i'll collect the microbench traces and post a follow-up. :+1:

profiling-bot: uploaded profile: /artifacts/profiles/2165432109/fa_v3_misaligned_512.tgz (10MB)
